#Sagility caught my eye because of all Mutual Fund buying and buy reports by Nomura, ICICI and Motilal along with it's Investor day meet! Below is an attempt to give you a balanced overview which you can use to further deep dive!

🏥 SAGILITY INDIA — THE AIRTIGHT 360° THESIS

Everything you need to know.
Every angle covered.
Every number verified.

A premium deep dive. 🧵

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

I. THE OPENING NUMBER

14.4x

That is the forward P/E you pay for
Sagility India at ₹41.8 on March 27, 2026.

FY28 consensus EPS = ₹2.9.
Three independent brokers. One answer.
(ICICI Securities. Motilal Oswal. Nomura.)
All three converge on ₹2.9.

PEG = 14.4x ÷ 29% EPS CAGR = 0.50x
(Below 1.0x = historically undervalued)

But a low multiple alone is not a thesis.
It is a question.

"Is the 14.4x a gift or a trap?"

This thread answers that question
from every angle — including the ones
that most bull theses deliberately skip.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

II. WHAT SAGILITY ACTUALLY IS

Most people think healthcare is doctors
and hospitals.

It is not.

Behind every medical decision in America
lives a $4.5 trillion administrative machine.

Every insurance claim → processed.
Every hospital procedure → authorized.
Every Medicare enrollment → managed.
Every improper payment → caught.
Every appeal → reviewed.

Someone has to do that work.

Sagility does it for the largest
healthcare organizations in America.

Pure-play US Healthcare BPO
(Business Process Outsourcing).

India's only listed company in this category.

Scale (March 2026, official PPT):

→ 80+ healthcare clients
→ 7 of the top 10 US health insurers
→ 3 of the top 6 PBMs
→ 18-year average client tenure
→ 97% client retention rate
→ 48,522 employees | 35 delivery centers
→ 1.37 BILLION transactions annually
→ 4,100+ clinicians on the payroll
→ 62–64% offshore (India + Philippines)
→ 25 years of healthcare domain expertise

The numbers that matter most:
18-year tenure. 97% retention.

These are not marketing metrics.
They are disclosed in SEBI-regulated
exchange filings. They mean:

Once a payer hires Sagility, they never leave.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

III. THE CHAINS THAT MADE IT UGLY

To understand the upside,
understand what happened first.

January 2022.
EQT (Swedish PE fund) carves Sagility out
of HGS for $1.2 billion.

Classic Leveraged Buyout (LBO):
Take a great business.
Load it with debt.
Extract value. IPO. Exit.

The debt they loaded:
FY24 Net Debt: $260 million (1.9x EBITDA)
FY24 Interest charge: ₹1,851 Crore
(40 cents of every EBITDA rupee → lenders!)

Return ratios in FY24 were embarrassing:
ROE: 3.6% | ROCE: 4.4% | ROIC: 4.7%

The stock looked mediocre.
The business underneath was not.

Then the chains began to snap.

FY25 Closing Debt: $122 million (-53%)
TTM Dec 2025 Debt: $71.5 million (-45%)
FY26E Debt: $63 million (per PPT)
FY27E Debt: $0

Fifteen thousand Crore of debt.
Gone in 30 months.

Return ratios as debt disappears (MOFSL):
FY27E: ROE 11.6% | ROCE 14.1% | ROIC 11.8%
FY28E: ROE 12.7% | ROCE 15.7% | ROIC 13.5%

From 3.6% to 12.7% ROE.

THIS is what post-LBO re-rating looks like.
And the market has not priced it.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

IV. THE NUMBERS (UNVARNISHED)

All from primary sources.
No cherry-picking. Both broker views shown.

Q3 FY26 (October–December 2025):

Revenue: $222.0 Mn USD (+29.1% cc)
In INR: ₹1,971 Cr (+35.7% — includes FX)

The real organic growth is 29.1% USD.
The 35.7% INR headline includes rupee impact.
Both are strong. Be precise on which you use.

Adj EBITDA: ₹513 Cr (26.0% margin)
Adj PAT: ₹323 Cr (+23% YoY)
Reported PAT: ₹268 Cr (post amortization)
Reported EPS: ₹0.57 | Adj EPS: ₹0.69

9-Month FY26 Scorecard:
Revenue: ₹5,169 Cr (+29.2% YoY)
Adj EBITDA: ₹1,316 Cr (25.5% margin)
Adj PAT: ₹824 Cr (+44.3% YoY)

FY26 Guidance (Raised Post Q3):
Revenue growth: 22.5% constant currency
Organic component: 13.8% cc
EBITDA margin: 24–25%

Revenue acceleration trend (USD):
Q1 FY25: $146.6M
Q2 FY25: $157.9M
Q3 FY25: $171.9M
Q4 FY25: $181.8M
Q1 FY26: $180.4M
Q2 FY26: $189.4M
Q3 FY26: $222.0M ← inflection!

Not just sustained. Accelerating.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

V. THE HONEST GROWTH DECOMPOSITION

Most bull theses stop at "35% revenue growth"
and move on. That is intellectually lazy.

Here is the breakdown:

LAYER 1 — TOP-5 CLIENT CORE
Revenue: $549.5M TTM Dec 2025
Growth: +9.9% YoY TTM
Quarterly trend: 9.3% → 6.9% → 9.5%

This is the bedrock. Sticky. Non-spectacular.
71% of revenue growing at ~10%.
That is the honest baseline.

LAYER 2 — MID-MARKET (BroadPath Effect)
Revenue: $166.0M TTM Dec 2025
Growth: +28.5% YoY TTM
Contribution to headline: ~$36.8M growth

The BroadPath acquisition ($58M, Jan 2025)
added 30+ new mid-market clients instantly.
This explains the headline acceleration.

LAYER 3 — ORGANIC MID-MARKET (New Wins)
13 new logos added organically in FY26
(Beyond BroadPath's acquired base)

Management-guided organic (ex-acquisitions):
13.8% constant currency for FY26

TOTAL PICTURE:
Headline ~28-35% = Core 10% + BroadPath
consolidation + FX + new organic wins.

From FY27: BroadPath enters the base.
Headline growth decelerates to 14–17%.
This is EXPECTED and means nothing bad.
Do not confuse comp base effect with
business deterioration.

CRITICAL CROSS-CHECK:
Revenue retention = 110.8%
(Clients growing their spend by 10.8%
above their starting point — net of all churn)

That single number proves: the business is
not just retaining clients. It is expanding.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

VI. THE BROADPATH ACQUISITION DECODED

January 29, 2025.
Sagility acquires BroadPath for $58 million.

Surface view: Mid-market US healthcare BPO.

Beneath the surface: A distribution network
+ a product called Synchrony.

WHAT SAGILITY BOUGHT:

→ 30+ new mid-market payer clients
  (zero overlap with existing base)
→ Entry to a 6th top-10 US insurer
→ 3 of top-6 PBMs added to roster
→ Medicare enrollment lifecycle capability
→ Bhive: WFH management platform
→ Access to the middle market — a segment
  Sagility had ZERO presence in before

The Cross-Sell Opportunity (Precise Data):

Mid-market client practice coverage:
(PPT verified — applies to ~54 mid-market
clients ONLY, not all 80 clients)

1 practice only: 63% → 30 clients
2 practices: 20% → ~13 clients
3 practices: 7.7% → ~5 clients
4 practices: 4.6% → ~3 clients
All 5 practices: 4.6% → ~3 clients

IMPORTANT PRECISION:
The top-7 national plan clients already
use 3–5 practices each. The cross-sell
runway is specifically in mid-market.
Apply this stat ONLY to BroadPath clients,
not to the entire 80-client universe.

But the math is still compelling:
Moving 15 mid-market clients from
1 practice → 3 practices = ~$60M ARR.
No new client acquisition needed.
Just selling what already exists.

FY27 is the cross-sell proof year.
If by Q2 FY27, clients are still at 63%
single-practice usage → flag the thesis.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

VII. THE SYNCHRONY MODEL
(The Most Underfollowed Growth Driver)

BroadPath brought more than clients.
It brought Synchrony.

Synchrony is NOT just integration.
It is a productized managed services model:

→ End-to-end PMPM-priced lifecycle
→ For mid-market Medicare Advantage plans
→ Covering: enrollment, claims, UM, PI
→ "Highly sticky — can survive M&A events"
→ "Higher wallet share as scope is end-to-end"

An actual Synchrony deal (PPT verified):

Before Synchrony:
Client total ops spend: $25M/year
Split: In-house $13.5M | Others $5.5M | Sagility $6M

After Synchrony:
Client total ops spend: $20M/year (saves $5M!)
All of it goes to Sagility Managed Services
New 5-year committed revenue: $70M total

For Sagility:
Revenue per client: $6M → $20M = 3.3x!
Client saves $5M. Sagility gets 3.3x revenue.
Both win.

If even 5 mid-market clients convert:
~$100M+ guaranteed annual revenue
On a committed, PMPM, 5-year contract.

ZERO of this is modelled in any broker forecast.
It is pure option value sitting unpriced.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

VIII. THE AI THESIS — COMPLETE AND HONEST

The first question every analyst asks:
"Can AI replace what Sagility does?"

Here is the full answer — including
the parts the bull thesis usually omits.

WHY FULL AI SUBSTITUTION IS IMPOSSIBLE:

US healthcare admin sits inside a
multi-layer compliance fortress:

HIPAA (Health Insurance Portability and
Accountability Act): Patient data cannot
touch OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, or any
public Large Language Model. Legally.

FCA (False Claims Act): Every claim
decision must be human-auditable.
Black-box AI = FCA liability.

CMS (Centers for Medicare and Medicaid
Services): Care decisions require
explainability. Not probabilistic outputs.

HITRUST + SOC 2: Security certifications
that take 2–4 years to build per center.

Result: US payers CANNOT legally use
ChatGPT or any public AI for healthcare
administration. They need a HIPAA-certified,
HITRUST-audited, FCA-compliant partner
with deep clinical workflow expertise.

Sagility took 25 years to build that.
That is not a product. That is an institution.

WHAT SAGILITY'S AI ACTUALLY DOES (Deployed):

SmarTec Nurse Assist:
96% AI accuracy. 100% with Human-in-Loop.
Clinician workload reduced: 25–35%
Care delivery: 18 hours faster
Prior authorization: SLM + LLM stack
Won: 2026 AI Excellence Award
Won: 2026 Augmented Intelligence Award

SmarTec Appeals Assist:
OCR + NLP + AI Knowledge Agent
Appeals timeline reduced: 2–3 days
Clinical ops efficiency: +25–35%
US appeals admin market: $2.5B (PPT figure)

Sagility Smart Step:
12% ER visit reduction
18% frailty claims reduction
22% inpatient admission reduction
5x ROI on long-term healthcare spend

Live production:
32 AI use cases | 10 active client deployments
(Up from 25 use cases in Q2 FY26 — growing fast)

THE PMPM PRICING SHIFT (The Real Prize):

Old pricing: ₹X per employee per month
New pricing: ₹X per member per month (PMPM)
Or: ₹X per outcome delivered (Value-based)

Why this matters for the P&L:

Under FTE pricing: AI reduces headcount
needed → Revenue FALLS as productivity rises.

Under PMPM pricing: Revenue tied to members
served, not people deployed. AI cuts cost.
Revenue stays constant. Margin EXPANDS.

Management confirmed the transition at
Analyst Day (March 25, 2026):
"Pricing model is a mix of transaction-based,
outcome-based, and FTE-based pricing."

HONEST ASSESSMENT:
The % of PMPM revenue is NOT disclosed.
This is a watch item and future catalyst.
It is NOT proven at scale yet.
PMPM is the bull case optionality.
Not the base case today.

If 20%+ revenue on PMPM by FY27:
+150 bps to EBITDA margin. P/E re-rates.
If PMPM stays < 5% of revenue:
The AI story is real but margin benefit delayed.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

IX. THE OBBBA — A POLICY THAT FEEDS SAGILITY

July 4, 2025.
President Trump signs the
One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA).

The financial media called it a disaster.
For US payers? Yes.
For Sagility? Read carefully.

WHAT THE OBBBA DOES:

→ $1 trillion in Medicaid cuts over 10 years
→ 11.8–13.7 million Americans lose coverage
→ ACA subsidies reduced: enrollment drops
→ NEW: Medicaid eligibility checks every 6 months
→ NEW: Work requirements for Medicaid recipients

WHAT THIS CREATES FOR PAYERS:

Every 6 months: millions of Medicaid members
must re-verify eligibility.
That means millions of:
→ Eligibility processing events
→ Enrollment and dis-enrollment transactions
→ Member communications
→ Appeals from wrongful denials

All of it = Sagility's core competency.
All of it = non-discretionary volume.

THE MECHANISM (Usually Missing from Theses):

Q3 FY26 open enrollment was "exceptional."
The 29.1% USD growth was real.
But WHY was it exceptional?

ACA's 29% new-consumer decline
forced existing beneficiaries to actively
switch plans during open enrollment.
Plan-switching = Sagility processes it.

More disruption = more switching = more work.
OBBBA is not a headwind. It is a workload surge.

EVIDENCE IN NUMBERS:
Sagility published a dedicated OBBBA white
paper (March 8, 2026) explaining how payers
can adapt their operations.

Translation: "We are the solution. Call us."

PAYER CEO QUOTES (directly from official PPT):

Humana CFO, Q4 2025:
"This includes EXPANDING OUTSOURCING
capabilities, simplifying and standardizing
processes..."

Elevance CEO, Q4 2025:
"We continue to view 2026 as a trough year.
Medicaid operating margin: -1.75%."

When payer CFOs say they are expanding
outsourcing to survive margin compression,
the analyst job is simple:
Find the outsourcer. That is Sagility.

THE MLR CRISIS (The $200-300B Story):

Medical Loss Ratio (MLR) = % of premium
spent on actual claims. Lower = better.

MLR trajectory for major US payers:
UHC: 82% → 88% | CVS Aetna: 84% → 92%
Humana: 87% → 90% | Centene: 88% → 92%
Elevance: 88% → 90% | Cigna HC: 82% → 84%

ACA regulatory ceiling: 85% for large plans.
CVS Aetna is 7 percentage points ABOVE ceiling.

Every payer is in a cost crisis.
MLR reduction opportunity: $200–300B.
(Source: Sagility official PPT, NSE filing)

Sagility's pitch: "We redesign your
Utilization Management processes with AI
and guarantee savings from Day 1."

This is not a future hope.
It is an active sales pipeline.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

X. THE FINANCIAL REALITY
(Both broker views. No hiding divergences.)

REVENUE (₹ Millions):

Year    ICICI     MOFSL    My Base

FY26E   71,241    73,265   72,000
FY27E   83,467    84,273   83,800
FY28E   94,425    96,085   95,000
CAGR:   ~19%      ~20%     ~19%

Note: MOFSL 2.8% higher due to FX assumptions.
Both are in a narrow, defensible range.

EBITDA MARGIN (%):

Year    ICICI    MOFSL    Honest Base
FY25A   22.6     23.3     23.0
FY26E   24.7     24.7     24.7 ← consensus!
FY27E   25.0     24.4     24.5

ICICI's 25.6% FY28E is above management
guidance of 24–25%. MOFSL's 24.4% is inside
management range. Base case: 24.5%.

REPORTED EPS (₹):

Year    ICICI    MOFSL    NOMURA

FY27E   2.30     2.40     ~2.3

⭐ ALL THREE BROKERS = ₹2.9 FY28E ⭐
This is the highest-confidence data point
in this entire thesis.

A NOTE ON REPORTED vs ADJUSTED EPS:
Adjusted EPS adds back amortization of
acquired intangibles (from the $1.2B LBO).
This gap (~₹0.45–0.50/share) persists
until December 2037 (confirmed in PPT).
BOTH are valid disclosure frames.
BOTH brokers use REPORTED EPS for P/E.
There is no hidden drag — already in models.

INTEREST EXPENSE COLLAPSE:
FY24: ₹1,851 Cr → FY25: ₹1,271 Cr
FY26E: ~₹1,018 Cr → FY27E: ~₹640–700 Cr
(Lease liabilities remain post-borrowing repayment)
FY28E: ~₹440–500 Cr

Every ₹100 Cr of interest saved = ₹65 Cr PAT.
The interest collapse alone explains
most of the 29% EPS CAGR.

CASH ACCUMULATION:
ICICI FY28E: ₹39,161 Mn = ₹8.37/share
MOFSL FY28E: ₹10,352 Mn = ₹2.21/share

Why the gap?
ICICI FY26E capex: ₹1,654 Mn
MOFSL FY26E capex: ₹6,049 Mn
9-Month actual capex: $15.4M → ₹1,703 Mn annualized

ICICI is closer to actuals.
Realistic FY28E cash: ₹25,000–35,000 Mn
= ₹5.3–7.5 per share
= 13–18% of today's market cap is future cash.

RETURN RATIOS (MOFSL, most detailed):
FY25: ROE 7.3% ROCE 8.9% ROIC 7.0%
FY26E: 11.3% | 13.0% | 11.0%
FY27E: 11.6% | 14.1% | 11.8%
FY28E: 12.7% | 15.7% | 13.5%

On ROCE: Sagility's PPT shows "54.9% ROCE."
This excludes goodwill and intangibles.
It reveals the underlying business earns
exceptional returns on operating capital.
But the $912M of LBO goodwill IS real capital.
Including it: ROCE = 11–16%.
Both numbers are true. Use 15.7% for
investment analysis. Use 54.9% for business
quality assessment.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

XI. THE SHAREHOLDER STRUCTURE
(Where the cheap valuation comes from)

Promoter Holdings:
June 2025: 67.4% (EQT, fully pledged for LBO)
September 2025: 67.4%
December 2025: 51.0% ← sold 16.4% in Q3!

The 16.4% single-tranche OFS (Offer for Sale)
by EQT in Q3 FY26 is THE reason the stock
fell from ₹58 to ₹36. A -38% crash.

Not a business issue.
Not an earnings issue.
A PE fund lifecycle issue.

EQT bought in 2022. Listed Nov 2024.
They need to return capital to LPs.
At 51% remaining, there are 1–2 more
tranches almost certainly coming.
Each tranche = temporary -10 to -20% crash.

BUT: Who absorbed the Q3 OFS?

DII holding: 14.9% → 21.4% (absorbed bulk!)
FII holding: 5.6% → 10.2% (nearly doubled!)
Others: 12.2% → 17.4%

Smart institutional money doubled their
position at ₹47.6 IPO and again post-OFS.
ICICI AMC, Morgan Stanley, Norges Bank
Norway — they did the work. They are holding.

The overhang is KNOWN and EXPECTED.
That is actually the ideal buying condition.

When EQT sells the final tranche:
The overhang is gone permanently.
The stock re-rates to intrinsic value.
That re-rating is the inflection point.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

XII. THE HONEST RISK REGISTER
(Six real risks. No sugarcoating.)

RISK 1 — EQT OVERHANG (CERTAIN, ACTIVE)
More selling is coming. 1–2 tranches left.
Each = -10 to -20% temporary drawdown.
Strategy: Use each OFS as a buying event.
DII/FII absorption capacity has been proven.

RISK 2 — TOP-5 DECELERATION (ACTIVE, WATCH)
Top-5 TTM growth: 9.9% (71% of revenue)
Quarterly trend: 9.3% → 6.9% → 9.5%
Two consecutive quarters below 7% = flag.
Monitor every earnings release.

RISK 3 — DSO ELEVATION (ACTIVE, MATERIAL)
Trade receivables: $148M → $184M in 9 months
ICICI models 74–76 days. Actuals = ~84 days.
If structural: FCF undershoots ICICI by
₹2,500–3,000 Mn. Q4 FY26 = critical test.

RISK 4 — BROADPATH CROSS-SELL TIMELINE
(LATENT — FY27 is proof year)
63% of mid-market clients on 1 practice only.
If still above 60% by September 2026:
The Synchrony/cross-sell thesis needs revision.
Specific metric to track quarterly.

RISK 5 — MARGIN CEILING (STRUCTURAL, PRICED)
Employee cost ratio rose 400 bps YoY.
Q3 FY25: 57.8% → Q3 FY26: 61.9%
BroadPath WFH workers cost 3–4x India rates.
This is WHY management guides 24–25%.
Already adjusted for. Not new. Priced in.
(Labour Code ongoing impact: 0.2% of revenue
= ₹150 Mn/year = immaterial, PPT confirmed.)

RISK 6 — AMORTIZATION TO FY38 (KNOWN, MANAGED)
LBO created ₹80,687 Mn in goodwill/intangibles.
Annual amortization: ~$16.5M until Dec 2037.
Post-tax drag: ~₹890 Mn/year from reported PAT.
Both brokers already model this in reported EPS.
Screener's 22.4x trailing vs forward 14.4x
is simply trailing vs 2-year forward — normal.
No hidden adjustment. Already in all numbers.
